AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Spinal lipomas are generally thought to occur as a result of failed primary neurulation. Failed primary neurulation allows invasion of mesenchymal tissue of mesodermic origin into the neural structure, leading to the formation of a spinal lipoma. Despite most spinal lipomas being regarded as the result of failed primary neurulation, some confusion in terms of the embryogenesis of spinal lipomas remains. Recently, a novel classification of spinal lipomas based on embryonic changes seen during primary and secondary neurulation was has been proposed.

AbstractText.Label: CASE DESCRIPTION
AbstractText.content: We present a case of an intradural-extramedullary spinal cord lipoma, associated with a subjacent subcutaneous lipoma at the cervicothoracic region. The patient presented with worsening neurologic symptoms, indicating ongoing cervical myelopathy. A subtotal resection along with posterior cervical stabilization was achieved, with mild improvement of neurologic symptoms. Clinical, pathological, and radiological records are reviewed.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first described case of a spinal cord lipoma with at such a location, and one that cannot be fully categorized within the newly proposed classification system.
